brief: 5 healthy client boundaries every freelancer should set — and how to communicate them.

slots.subtitle: Five healthy limits that protect your energy, your craft, and your client relationships without guilt or friction.
slots.author: The Freelance Co.
The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Healthy limits are not walls; they are the structure that keeps projects on track and creativity flowing. Without them, resentment grows and output suffers.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Publish your response times and stick to them. Clients will respect predictable availability more than an inbox that promises instant replies around the clock.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Document deliverables before you begin. When extra requests arrive, present a change order calmly so scope creep becomes a paid upgrade, not a free favor.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Require a deposit and enforce clear invoicing schedules. Discussing money early removes awkward surprises and signals that you treat your business seriously.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Include two rounds of feedback in your contract. Additional changes should trigger a conversation about timeline and budget, protecting both your schedule and sanity.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Frame every boundary as a policy that serves the work. A kind, confident tone builds trust and removes the guilt from saying no.

slots.author: The Freelance Co.
slots.body: Pick one boundary and add it to your next proposal. Small shifts today create sustainable freelance careers tomorrow.
